tickets.title: Four gate flakes wait on events, not fixed deadlines
tickets.what: Land gates 2026-11-22 each needed an immediate rerun for: (a) hud-watch-async 'read-close preflight: external close' and (b) job-retention 'an unreadable job.json counts as possibly open until it can be read' — both `AssertionError: watcher condition did not settle` from `until` in tests/helpers/job-retention-fixture.mjs:75 after ~5.1 s (excerpt: ~/.hud/flows/f87f184a7bbf6b792.json.gate-1.log); (c) sonic-process 'sonic checkpoints reach the caller and keep the original pi process running'; (d) fs-wait 'waitUntilFs wakes within 100 ms of a file change and closes all watchers'. Under the parallel full suite fixed deadlines (5 s settle, 100 ms wake) are too tight. For each: wait on the real event or scale the deadline to load, and if a test asserts latency (100 ms), keep the product promise but measure it in a way that load cannot break (e.g. relative to when the watcher was armed, or a separate perf check). Fix a real product gap in the product, not the test.

acceptance.text: Cause named per test (fixture timing vs product)
Each of the four passes 20 consecutive runs alongside a parallel `npm run test:mjs` (command and counts in the report)
No test loses what it asserts; a latency claim stays tested

tickets.title: Watcher-reap read-close flake and install-claude umask dependence
tickets.what: (1) Land gate f2ce3cf718a51d534 needed a rerun for `read-close: rejected CLI quit keeps closed while the watcher retries terminal reap` (tests/unit/thin-mcp-watcher-reap.test.mjs); gate f4d39157cd57a8c2c needed it again plus three more: `watcher reaps an exited root without a snapshot once (missing or renamed tab), idles, then archives it at retention` (tests/unit/hud-watch-async.test.mjs), `Claude outside herdr shows no workers from another pane` (tests/unit/native-statusline.test.mjs), `question, follow-up and land repair reopen the same tabless pi session; expiry starts a headless repair` (tests/unit/thin-mcp-headless.test.mjs). Gate logs: ~/.hud/flows/f2ce3cf718a51d534.json.gate-1.log, ~/.hud/flows/f4d39157cd57a8c2c.json.gate-1.log. First look for a shared cause (a common test helper with a fixed deadline or poll interval) and fix it once there; then per-case. Same approach as test-flakes/01 and 03: find the fixed deadline or ordering assumption that breaks under parallel load, replace it with an event/condition wait, keep the assertion. (2) tests/unit/install-claude.test.mjs:114 expects mode 0640 and gets 0600 in worker environments (seen by two workers; the gate passes), so the expectation depends on the process umask. Make the test set or derive the umask so it passes under any umask, without weakening what it checks about the installed file's mode.

tickets.title: Sweep fixed short waits in watcher and MCP tests
tickets.what: test-flakes/01-07 fixed ~20 gate flakes one by one; nearly every one was a fixed inner deadline (5-10 s or a 200-350 ms sleep) that breaks under parallel load. test-flakes/07's report (job j3b98819a7df56764, hud_read it) lists the remaining explicit sub-10 s waits by file:line across tests/unit/thin-mcp-*.test.mjs, job-retention*, hud-watch*, plus tests/helpers/job-retention-fixture.mjs:73 whose bare waits inherit a 5 s limit. Sweep them in one pass: helpers' default waits follow the enclosing test signal (60 s test timeout) instead of a short fixed limit; sleeps used as 'nothing happened' checks become waits on a later observable event (a watcher summary, a status query) as test-flakes/07 did. Keep every assertion and every product timing bound (e.g. 'within 200 ms', configured graces). Split into two commits if large (helpers first, then call sites).

acceptance.text: No fixed sub-10 s wait remains as a correctness bound in the listed files unless it is a product bound, which the report lists with the reason

tickets.title: Supervisor rest test counts the watcher's subscribe-time pane.get
tickets.what: `tests/unit/thin-mcp-cli-process.test.mjs:171` ("supervisor events: 60s at rest …") failed in two land gates on 2026-11-25 (f62da6fce5ec7a353, f9c65084a5e61a70c) and passed on rerun. Failure: the rest window saw `pane.get {pane_id}` before the expected `agent.get` calls (`assert.ok(extra.every(r => r.method === 'agent.get'))` at :198). Since herdr-fork/04 the watcher reconciles direct-exec roots (`runtime.reconcileTabs()` after its `hud-watch` subscribe reply, `probeDirectRoot` → `pane.get`), and the baseline waits only for the subscribe request to be sent, not for that reconciliation. Find the actual source of the `pane.get` and make the test wait for it to finish before snapshotting (or attribute requests to the supervisor vs watcher), without weakening the at-rest guarantee for the supervisor. If the request comes from the supervisor during rest, it is a product bug: fix the supervisor instead.

acceptance.text: Report names the code path that issued the pane.get
The test passes 30 consecutive runs under `TZ=UTC node tests/run-mjs.mjs 8`-level load (e.g. 8 parallel copies), with the supervisor's zero-spawn/zero-STATUS-write assertions unchanged
